subtitle: Where deeper industrial integration creates strategic value, through which instruments, and where to stay out

inlines.v: Solar Manufacturing: Wafers (Japan->Korea). Permanent Magnets & Drive Systems: Rare-earth oxides & compounds (joint); Rare-earth permanent magnets (Japan->Korea). Battery Materials & Cells: Natural graphite (joint); Cobalt intermediates & chemicals (joint); Lithium chemicals (joint); Battery materials (foil, electrolyte) (Japan->Korea). Grid Equipment & Conductors: Electric Grid refining (joint). Semiconductors & Power Electronics: Electric Grid components (Japan->Korea).

Recognise trusted partner supply of electric vehicles refining (rare-earth metals, rare-earth oxides & compounds) in procurement and content rules. Common anti-circumvention rules for batteries refining (battery materials (foil, electrolyte), cathode materials & precursors, cobalt intermediates & chemicals) and wind refining (copper wire & rod, rare-earth metals, rare-earth oxides & compounds) and rare-earth oxides & compounds and cobalt intermediates & chemicals and lithium chemicals. Bind market access for wafers, rare-earth permanent magnets. Keep pgms (iridium, ruthenium); copper ores & concentrates; nickel intermediates & chemicals open to global sourcing.
Upgrade Korea-Japan Supply Chain Partnership Arrangement and Industrial and Trade Policy Dialogue: sector strategy, reciprocal commitments, a KPI dashboard and an annual review. No new MOU.
Do not co-subsidise new Coal components capacity. Do not co-subsidise new Accumulator parts & separators capacity. Do not co-subsidise new Coal assembly capacity.

Of 142 technology x stage cells and electro-industrial nodes assessed for the pair, 33 show an active complementarity (a supplier meeting the other's need, a shared chokepoint, a capacity-constrained trusted supplier or a chain specialisation), 6 direct competition and 78 no strategic case. The relationship is not one of general similarity: most of the electro-industrial base needs no bilateral intervention.

AIB strategic roles: Japan Capital & Investment Anchor (primary), Specialized Technology & Manufacturing Anchor (primary), Scale Manufacturing & Integration Platform (primary), Coordination / Bridge Hub (secondary); Korea Specialized Technology & Manufacturing Anchor (primary), Scale Manufacturing & Integration Platform (primary), Coordination / Bridge Hub (secondary), Capital & Investment Anchor (secondary).

Korea supplies solar cells, cathode materials & precursors, gallium, germanium & indium, non-oriented electrical steel (ngo) where Japan is short; Japan supplies wafers, rare-earth permanent magnets, battery materials (foil, electrolyte), piezo-electric quartz where Korea is short; the two share exposure to the same coercive supplier in rare-earth oxides & compounds, natural graphite, cobalt intermediates & chemicals, lithium chemicals, polysilicon, where neither can supply the other and the answer is joint demand, finance and third-country capacity.

From the AIB roles, Japan brings capital, specialised technology and manufacturing, scale manufacturing; Korea brings specialised technology and manufacturing, scale manufacturing, coordination across allied chains. Public finance runs through JBIC, NEXI, JOGMEC on the Japan side and KEXIM, K-SURE, KOMIR, KDB on the Korea side. The trade is market access and demand certainty for trusted capacity.

Do not co-subsidise new Coal components capacity: both are strong suppliers (Japan 9%, Korea 6%). Trusted supply is adequate: this is commercial competition.

Do not co-subsidise new Coal assembly capacity: both are strong suppliers (Japan 5%, Korea 4%). Trusted supply is adequate: this is commercial competition.

. Gaps: no cross-sector KPI dashboard or review cycle; no bilateral mechanism covers SC-SOLAR, SC-SEMIS; JPKR-M1 has no published project pipeline.
Do not sign a new energy MOU. Give JPKR-M1 a sector strategy, reciprocal commitments and a KPI dashboard covering the recommended compacts, reviewed every 12 months.

This section sets out what already exists before anything new is proposed. Facts are from the curated evidence layer (accessed 2026-11-06); items marked partial or unverified rest on secondary sources and should be confirmed before citation.
Korea's memberships in OSI's economic-security agreements table: IPEF, MSP, U.S. FTA.
DFAT notes RCEP entered into force for Korea on 1 Feb 2022 and may be used by exporters as an alternative to KAFTA; the member list shown here is partial.
The 16 Mar 2023 Tokyo summit restored shuttle diplomacy, with Japan pledging to lift its three-material curbs and Korea to drop its WTO case.

Korean and Japanese officials agreed a close cooperation system on critical-mineral supply risks, support for company and agency cooperation on joint development in third countries (Latin America, Asia, Africa), and policy coordination in the Minerals Security Partnership and IEA; no projects were named.

The dialogue, set up Feb 2024 with a first meeting in Jun 2024, held its second meeting in Tokyo on 26 Mar 2025 and agreed to develop a Japan-ROK cooperation platform for hydrogen and ammonia supply chains; the METI page could not be opened.
Senior officials meeting in New York agreed to enhance dialogue on critical minerals and cooperation in Southeast Asia and Sub-Saharan Africa through the trilateral Early Warning System.
At the October 2025 Tokyo conference the two business federations agreed Korea's CPTPP participation was important given US protectionism and supply-chain disruption.

The second round discussed a joint response to falling copper treatment and refining charges, cooperation within the Minerals Security Partnership and ways to develop critical minerals jointly in third countries; no agreement or named project was reported.

On 13 Jan 2026 the leaders discussed supply-chain cooperation in depth and agreed to launch agency-level talks on economic security cooperation, with rare-earth stabilisation reported as a focus; no outputs were published.
The US-hosted ministerial in Feb 2026 was attended by Japan and Korea among others, and Korea was reported to chair the FORGE critical-minerals forum through June 2026.

Korea chaired the Minerals Security Partnership until June 2026; a February 2026 report says its 17 members carried into the successor FORGE; Korean public lenders joined the MSP Finance Network; no signed US-Korea critical-minerals MOU was found.

A standing consultative body launched 14 Mar 2026 to review trade cooperation, economic security, supply chains, steel and mineral resources; the same article reports plans for joint exploration and investment in critical minerals and shared market monitoring; no schedule published.

The 19 May 2026 trade-ministry release covers crude oil swaps and mutual supply in a crisis, deeper LNG cooperation under the KOGAS-JERA agreement, SCPA crisis mechanisms and regional reserves via Japan's proposed POWERR Asia; no projects or funding named; hydrogen and critical minerals not covered.

In June 2026 Korea's trade ministry said no decision had been made on applying to CPTPP after reports of a late-June application; Japan reportedly would back accession without first requiring Korea to lift its Fukushima seafood ban; the Japan position is a press report.

The joint statement backs coordination on resource procurement and supply-chain stability, support for Korea's CPTPP accession, hydrogen certification and safety standards, critical-mineral stockpiling and crisis response through the SCPA, and an early resumption of the Korea-US-Japan Business Dialogue; business statement, not binding.
In the OSI energy basket, Japan imported US$10.2bn from Korea and Korea imported US$10.7bn from Japan (bilateral flows 2024, summed over the technology x stage cells).

RCEP entered into force for Japan on 1 Jan 2022 and for Korea on 1 Feb 2022, giving the two countries a shared preferential trade framework with no separate bilateral FTA; tariff schedules not reviewed.

From July 2019 Japan required individual licences for fluorinated polyimide, photoresist and hydrogen fluoride exports to Korea and removed Korea from its white list; Korea removed Japan from its own list in Aug 2019 and filed a WTO complaint; Japan lifted the three-item curbs in Mar 2023.

Korea completed procedures to drop its 2019 WTO complaint on 23 Mar 2023, a week after the 16 Mar Yoon-Kishida summit; Japan had pledged to lift the three-material curbs; the article does not confirm the curbs had by then been lifted.

The three leaders agreed to pilot an early warning system exchanging supply-chain information via embassies in selected countries, with critical minerals and rechargeable batteries as priority products, plus an annual commerce and industry ministers track; the system is not published as operating beyond the pilot.
KNOC reportedly signed an MOU with JOGMEC in February 2025 on cooperation in hydrogen, ammonia and CCS.

Ministers Kim Jung-kwan and Akazawa signed the SCPA in Tokyo on 14 Mar 2026: early notification of disruptions, an emergency meeting within five days of a request, and prior consultation before measures that could harm the other side; no amounts or named projects.
Investment vehicle, project pipeline and financing
Corporate relationships in the recommended compacts
LGES agreed to supply Toyota's North American EVs with about 20 GWh a year of modules from 2025, with roughly 4 trillion won (about 3 billion dollars) invested in Michigan lines dedicated to Toyota.
JERA and Lotte Fine Chemical agreed in Aug 2024 to develop low-carbon hydrogen and ammonia fuel supply chains, with joint studies on commercial frameworks and ammonia bunkering at Yokohama.

Sumitomo Chemical plans EUV and ArF photoresist production in Korea, previously made only in Osaka, with about 30 billion yen invested across Korea and Japan; site and start date undecided; dollar figure is a rough conversion.

OCI and Tokuyama hold 50:50 in OCI Tokuyama Semiconductor Materials, which broke ground in Sarawak in July 2025 on an 8,000 tonne a year plant targeting commercial operation in 2029; semiconductor-grade, not solar-grade; amount not stated.

The 2023 Honda-LGES joint venture L-H Battery keeps operating its Ohio cell plant under a lease after LGES sold the building to Honda for about 4.22 trillion won (2.85 billion dollars) announced Dec 2025; a later report of a lower closing value of 3.74 trillion won is unconfirmed.
LGES agreed to sell the Ohio JV factory building and related assets to Honda for about $2.85B with the JV continuing via lease and closing targeted for 2026-02-28.

JERA and Samsung C&T signed a two-year initial MoU on 6 Jul 2026 to explore resilience and supply security in hydrogen and ammonia value chains, including storage and ammonia trading; exploratory, no amounts.

Samsung's advanced-packaging R&D lab opened in Yokohama's Minato Mirai district in Sept 2026 per a Herald report, after a Dec 2023 plan of about 40 billion yen (280 million dollars); investment figures vary across reports and Japanese materials makers are named partners.
Unverified items are left out of this section; they stay in the evidence register (evidence_register.csv) and the evidence layer.

Working channels today: Japan-ROK Hydrogen and Ammonia Cooperation Dialogue and company links (a project pipeline). What the relationship lacks: no cross-sector KPI dashboard or review cycle; no bilateral mechanism covers SC-SOLAR, SC-SEMIS; JPKR-M1 has no published project pipeline.
